title: Central Italy
subtitle: Marche, Abruzzo, Umbria and Lazio
objectives: Describe the main wines of central Italy
Name key grapes of the Adriatic coast
Explain the role of Verdicchio and Montepulciano

steps.title: The Adriatic side
steps.body: On the Adriatic coast, Marche and Abruzzo dominate. Marche's Verdicchio, from Castelli di Jesi and Matelica, gives crisp, almond-scented whites that can age well. Abruzzo's Montepulciano gives deep, soft, plummy reds, and its rosé is called Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo. Conero, near Ancona, makes structured Montepulciano reds.

steps.title: Umbria and Lazio
steps.body: Umbria, landlocked, has Orvieto, a white blend led by Grechetto and Trebbiano, and Montefalco Sagrantino, one of the most tannic red grapes in the world. Lazio, around Rome, is known for Frascati, a light white from Malvasia and Trebbiano. Altitude and volcanic soils help keep these wines fresh.

steps.prompt: Match each wine to its region.
steps.explanation: Central Italy offers distinct wines on both sides of the Apennines.

steps.body: Verdicchio is one of Italy's best-value whites. Good ones, like Castelli di Jesi Riserva, gain honey and almond notes with five years in bottle.

steps.prompt: Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo is a rosé made from the ____ grape.
steps.explanation: Montepulciano's deep colour gives Cerasuolo its cherry-red hue.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Marche's Verdicchio is a crisp, age-worthy white
Abruzzo's Montepulciano gives soft reds and Cerasuolo rosé
Umbria has Sagrantino and Orvieto; Lazio has Frascati
